articles.title: AP rolls out comprehensive action plan to combat El Niño impact - The Hans India
articles.full_text:
Amaravati: With Andhra Pradesh witnessing a significant rainfall deficit during southwest monsoon, Agriculture Minister Kinjarapu Atchannaidu has directed officials to implement a comprehensive action plan to safeguard crops and support farmers against the impact of El Niño conditions.
Addressing a webinar with Agriculture and allied department field officials on Sunday, the Minister instructed officials to focus on crop protection, soil moisture conservation, promotion of alternative crops, emergency seed availability, and climate-resilient farming practices.
He said State has recorded a 53.7 per cent rainfall deficit during the current southwest monsoon season. Against the normal rainfall of 225.7 mm expected by this time, the State has received only 104.5 mm. Of the 28 districts, 21 are facing rainfall deficit, while West Godavari, Annamayya, East Godavari, Visakhapatnam, Chittoor, and Prakasam have been categorised under severe rainfall deficit. Only Nellore has recorded normal rainfall.
At mandal level, 249 mandals are experiencing severe rainfall deficit, while 359 mandals fall under the rainfall deficit category.
The Minister noted that as of July 25, crop sowing in 12 districts had covered less than 50% of normal area. The situation is particularly critical in Annamayya (9%), Bapatla (5%), Prakasam (15%), and Markapuram (15%).
Against the normal kharif crop area of 30.84 lakh hectares, crops have been sown in 16.35 lakh hectares so far. While paddy, soybean, and cotton have shown relatively better progress, cultivation of groundnut, sunflower, sorghum, and horse gram remains significantly behind schedule.
The Minister directed officials to implement alternative crop planning and emergency seed distribution in mission mode. He said 14,078 quintals of contingency seeds, including red gram, green gram, foxtail millet, black gram, and sesame, have already been arranged through the AP State Seed Development Corporation, with additional stocks available at Acharya NG Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) and Krishi Vigyan Kendras.
He said 26,950 quintals of seeds would be required by July 31 for high-risk areas in Anantapur, Kurnool, and Markapuram, while another 95,838 quintals would be needed by August 15 for 429 mandals across 21 districts.
Atchannaidu instructed officials to establish a 24x7 State El Niño Crop Protection Mission with a dedicated control room integrating weather forecasts, satellite information, water availability, crop status, water availability and field reports.
Officials were also directed to disseminate weather and crop advisories regularly through WhatsApp groups, Farmer Service Centres, television, radio, newspapers, IVRS, SMS, and the ICC Helpline (155251).
The Minister instructed district officials to coordinate with Irrigation Department to identify tail-end ayacut areas facing water shortages and encourage farmers to shift from long-duration paddy to suitable alternative crops wherever necessary.
He also stressed the need to promote micro-irrigation, protective irrigation, mulching, farm ponds, mechanisation, drought-resistant seeds, and other climate-resilient technologies through targeted subsidies.
Officials were asked to intensify awareness campaigns on crop insurance. The last date for enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) for all notified kharif crops except paddy is July 31, while the deadline for paddy is August 15.
Reassuring farmers, Atchannaidu said there was no need for panic, as the government is continuously monitoring the evolving weather situation and is committed to extending all necessary support to protect crops and farmers’ livelihoods.
